about: The plan for the lines of docs/woodex-os/14-PRODUCTION-TODO.md that are not done: a short title for each, the rounds in which the lines that can start now are done, and for each of those lines what is built and how it is tested. Read with the list by scripts/verify-plan.mjs, which writes docs/woodex-os/21-PENDING-WORK-PLAN-AND-TESTS.md and fails when the three disagree. When a line is done, take it out of its round and out of the titles.

rounds.name: The shop reads its products from `/api/v1`, behind a switch that stays off
rounds.why: P1, and the owner's word of 19 November ("start as you recommend", DL-037). Website Studio and Marketing, 17 of the 36 destinations of Feature status that are not open, wait for this line and then for the page builder (T-115); the Orders screen waits for it too. It is the first address of `/api/v1` in pages and the first that hands out money, so the rules of T-063 are tried on it before anything else is built on them.

lines.found: Read in the code on 19 November; nothing of it is built. The shop reads its products from its own Node API (`/api/products`, and `/api/products/overrides` for changed prices and stock), which reads the shop's database: the 148 sample products (D-007). Categories, series and pictures it can already read from `/api/v1`, through two bridges of the Node API, behind a switch that is off. `/api/v1` has no address for products. Laravel keeps each of the 170 real products as a draft and a published copy; all 170 are drafts, and publishing one asks for a review, a category, a price, a description, the shipping and warranty texts, a picture with its description, and a preview seen by the person who publishes (D-009, T-090). The basket prices its lines from the sales catalogue by the shop's own product number, not from these products.
build: `GET /api/v1/catalogue/products`, in pages, and one product by its address: only the published copy of a product that is not archived, never the draft. Prices as whole paisa with the currency, times in UTC, the filters the contract names (category, series, changed since) and no other. Written into `platform/resources/api/v1.openapi.json` and document 29 first.
The pictures of a published product at an address of their own, as the categories' pictures are.

A bridge in the shop's Node API and a reader in the React shop that turn the answer into the product the pages use today, behind a switch of the shop that stays off. With the switch off the shop reads exactly what it reads today.
How a basket of products read from Laravel is priced: the round decides it, records the decision, and a test sends such a basket.
tests: The contract test names the new routes, and each answer is compared with the contract key by key: success, a page beyond the last, a filter that is not allowed (400), a product that is not published (404), too many requests (429).
A draft, a withdrawn product and an archived one are never handed out, by the list or by their own address; what is handed out is the published copy, also when the draft was changed after it.
Money arrives as whole paisa; a product without a price is "on request" and carries no figure; a sale price is handed out only between its two dates.

The shop's reader is run against the answers the contract documents, in CI's `build-and-test`, and against a real answer of Laravel on the rehearsal: the same name, price and pictures arrive in the product the pages use.
With the switch off the shop asks Laravel nothing: its build and its existing scripts give what they gave before.
After the merge the outside check asks the products address on the live demo.
browser: On the rehearsal a product is published in the admin by a browser. The shop's bridge, pointed at that rehearsal, hands it to the shop's reader, and the product is shown with its name, price and picture. Withdrawn in the admin, it is gone from the shop.
lines.against: With the draft handed out in place of the published copy, the test of the unpublished product names it; with the shop's reader left reading rupees where paisa arrive, its script names the price.
lines.back: The shop's switch stays off: the live shop reads what it reads today, and the round changes no setting of either Vercel project. The new addresses hand out only published products, and none is published on the demo. The Node catalogue is not closed in this round.

rounds.name: On a phone, the key lists are cards
rounds.why: P1, and the line it waited for is done (T-041). The page of a list is never wider than a phone, but the list inside it is: a person scrolls sideways within the leads list to reach a lead's stage. The shared table is the one place to put that right for every list.

lines.found: Measured in a browser on 19 November, on the rehearsal at 390 px, as the owner. Leads: all eight columns are drawn; the table is 1,036 px wide in a frame of 356 px. Invoices: four of six columns, 391 px in 356. Quotations: three of six columns, and it fits. Tasks is not a table and fits. Projects (363 px in 356), Users (837 px) and the Receivables report (916 px) scroll inside their frame too; the line does not name them. Leads, Quotations and Projects draw the shared table; Invoices still writes its own.
build: The shared table learns a second way to draw its rows for a narrow screen: below 640 px a row is a card, with the cell that names the row on top, the cells the list marks as main under it, each with its heading, and the row's action. The list says which cells are main; a cell that is left off a card is left off on purpose.
Leads, Quotations and Invoices use it; Invoices moves to the shared table first. Tasks is measured again and left as it is if it still fits.
Choosing rows, and what can be done with all chosen, stay within reach on a card.
tests: A test draws a list in the narrow way and reads each card as a screen reader does: the row's name, each main fact with its heading ("Stage: Contacted", not a bare word), the action.
For each of the three lists: the cards are the same rows, in the same order, with the same links, as the table.
The count of views that write a table by hand falls by one (Invoices).
browser: At 390 px each of the four lists is measured: no frame inside the page scrolls sideways, and the page does not.
A journey step, on a phone: a lead is opened from its card and moved to another stage.
lines.against: With the narrow way taken off the leads list, the measurement at 390 px names the frame that scrolls.
lines.back: Views and styles only; the built stylesheet changes. Each list in its own commit, and the wide table is untouched.

rounds.name: The shop's database: its functions and the map of its tables
rounds.why: One reading of the live database serves both lines. T-175 is P1, and the two lines about moving data wait for it (T-176, T-177).

lines.found: Read from the live database on 17 November, 20:04 UTC: its public schema holds nine functions and one aggregate, and none has a fixed search path (defect D-029). Six of the functions come from the numbered migrations; three functions and the aggregate from the base schema file. None belongs to an extension. Only the database's owner can create objects there, so nothing can be put in their way today.
build: Migration 021 sets the search path of each of the nine functions, named one by one, with its rollback file.

The aggregate (`group_concat`) is expected to take no search path of its own in PostgreSQL; its two helper functions do. That is tried on the test database first, and the defect's text then says what was found.
It is applied to the live database as migration 020 was: the tests first, then one transaction together with its row in the ledger, then a reading back.
tests: On the PostgreSQL test database, after every migration no function of the public schema is without a search path, and the same test fails for a function added later without one. The rollback brings the earlier state back; applying twice changes nothing.
The old system's module tests pass on PostgreSQL with 021 applied (CI).
After it is applied: read back from the live database, no function is without a search path and the ledger has 21 rows; asked from outside, the shop still serves its products.
lines.against: With one function left out of the migration, the first test names it.
lines.back: No row changes, and the rollback file is tested: that is the safe way back your condition asks for (DL-028). No backup is known to exist (T-187).

lines.found: Read from the live database on 17 November, 20:04 UTC: 73 tables. 72 of them are the tables of the old system's schema files, name for name; the 73rd is the ledger that the migration tool keeps. None is missing and none is unknown. Laravel's migrations create 118 tables.
build: One file with a row for each old table: where it goes in Laravel, or that it is not moved and why; the module that owns it; its wave.
The same table as a document, written from the file.
The names of the live database's tables are read again when the map is written, reading only, and compared with the files.
tests: A check fails when a table of the old schema files is missing from the file or named twice, when a target table is not created by any Laravel migration, or when a wave is not a wave of the list.
A table that the live database has and the map does not know is named by the comparison and listed in the round's report.
lines.against: With one row taken out of the file, the check names the table.
lines.back: A document and a check. Nothing runs against any data.

rounds.name: Packages, the demo's housekeeping, the documents the code points at
rounds.why: Small lines, P2 and P3, taken together. They stand here and not at the end because packages fall further behind with every week, and because every later merge then adds a reading of a cold start.

lines.found: By the audit of 17 November (defect D-028): Composer reports one low advisory (Laravel 13.39; corrected in 13.40) and npm eleven moderate ones in the shop's build tools. None fails the audit today, which stops at high. The sandbox cannot reach Composer's package index: on 17 November four packages were moved in the lock file itself, and CI proved the result on a clean machine.
build: Laravel to 13.40 or newer, with what it then requires, and the other Composer packages to their newest corrected versions.
npm: the corrections that stay inside the same major version. For `react-router`, whose correction is a new major version, either the move with the shop's own tests, or a written reason to wait.

The audit gets a written list of accepted advisories, each with its reason. From then on an advisory of any severity that is not on the list fails the audit. Every Monday the audit also prints which packages have a newer version; that is read at the start of a round.
tests: The whole Laravel suite on SQLite and on MySQL; both journeys and the crawl of every screen.
The React shop's gate: build, types, its API and row-level-security tests on PostgreSQL, its browser acceptance.
`composer audit` and `npm audit` report nothing that is not on the list of accepted advisories.
browser: Both journeys and every screen on the new versions, as in every round.
lines.against: With the reason of one accepted advisory taken out of the list, the audit fails and names the advisory.
lines.back: Putting the lock files back. The React shop is built with other versions of its tools afterwards: the release report names every package that moves, before the merge.
lines.unknown: How Composer's own update is run where the sandbox cannot reach the package index: in the lock file itself, as on 17 November, or by a job in GitHub that commits the lock. It is decided when tried.

lines.found: The stylesheet is sent with `max-age=0, must-revalidate` (read on the live demo on 17 November, 19:21 UTC), so a browser asks for it again on every page. The names of the built files carry a mark of their content: a changed file has a new name.
build: In `platform/vercel.json` and its copy: one year and `immutable` for the files under `/build/assets/` only. The pages and the list of built files stay as they are.
tests: A test reads `vercel.json`: the long life is on the files with a marked name only. The two copies stay the same byte for byte (CI checks that today).
The outside check, which prints the stylesheet's header today, requires one year after the merge.
lines.against: With the header taken out of `vercel.json`, the test fails. On the branch the outside check still reads `max-age=0`, because the live site is the old one; after the merge it must read one year.
lines.back: A file with a marked name never changes under that name, so a long life cannot serve an old file. One line to put back.

lines.found: By the measurement in document 13: the function Vercel runs holds 226 MB of the 250 MB allowed; 153 MB of it is Vercel's PHP runtime.
build: The CI job that builds the demo as Vercel does prints the size of the function and fails above 240 MB.
tests: The job itself, tried once with the limit set below today's size.
lines.against: With the limit at 200 MB the job fails and names the size.
lines.back: A check only.

lines.found: Warm, the sign-in page's first byte comes after 0.08 to 0.17 s from a GitHub runner, by the list; 0.13 s on 17 November, 19:21 UTC. A cold start has never been measured, and no answer says whether the function was started for it.
build: The entry file marks an answer for which the function had to be started. It knows: its working folder under `/tmp` is not there yet. So a cold start is read, not guessed.
The outside check times its very first request by itself and prints whether it carried the mark.
tests: On the rehearsal: the first answer after a start carries the mark, the second does not.
Three cold readings from the live demo, with their dates, are written into `13-VERCEL-DEPLOYMENT.md`.
lines.against: With the mark taken out of the entry file, the rehearsal's test fails.
lines.back: One header on an answer, and a line of output.

lines.found: Read again on 18 November, 04:21 UTC, and corrected: until then this said that no timed run had ever started. GitHub's list holds one timed run, 44176315991, of 17 November, 21:06 UTC: green, 41 of 41 for the admin and 14 of 14 for the shop, started 2 h 43 min after the time due (18:23 UTC). The time due before it (12:23 UTC) and the one after it (00:23 UTC on 18 November) brought no run. So the timer works, and GitHub starts it late or drops it: one run in three times due. The check after a merge has run every time. Starting the check by hand is refused to this session (HTTP 403, tried on 17 November, 19:54 UTC).
build: GitHub's list of timed runs is read at the start of every round, and how many of the times due brought a run is written into the list.
If fewer than three of the last four times due brought a run, the timer is written again on `main` at another minute, and the list is read after the next times due.
tests: Runs started by the timer are in GitHub's list for at least three of the last four times due, and they are green.
lines.against: Done on 17 November: a forced failure opened issue #38, and the next proof closed it.
lines.back: Nothing changes on any site.

lines.found: Pull request #29 of 9 November (deliveries in the old dashboard) is still open. Its work entered `main` eight minutes after it was opened, as commit `e82b386`. Its migration, its rollback file and its screen are in `main` byte for byte; what it adds to its other files is in `main` too, but for 26 lines in places `main` has rewritten since. GitHub reports it as conflicting.
build: It is closed with a comment that says where its work is. Its branch is left as it is.
tests: GitHub lists no open pull request but the round's own.
lines.against: Nothing to take away: it is one action, read back from GitHub.
lines.back: A closed pull request can be opened again.

lines.found: Counted in `platform/app`, `routes`, `config`, `resources`, `database`, `tests` and `bootstrap`: 37 decisions named by number 108 times (D-58 the most), 200 mentions of a numbered document of the Interior studio (docs/09, docs/14 and docs/06 the most), 642 mentions of 120 requirement codes in seventeen families (QUO, CRM, WAP, PRJ and others). None of these documents is in this repository. Read against the archive the owner attached on 18 November: 119 of the 120 requirement codes are in the studio's requirements document and 31 of the 37 decisions in its decisions document; of the other six, four are named in other documents of the studio, two in none (D-111, D-112). The documents are also in the studio's public repository `woodex420/woodexinterior` at `603428c`, the commit this admin was copied from.
build: Three documents copied unchanged from that commit into `docs/laravel-os/source/`: the decisions (`07-DECISIONS.md`), the requirements (`02-MASTER-PRD.md`) and the Hostinger guide (`06-DEPLOYMENT-HOSTINGER.md`). Each gets a first paragraph that says whose system it describes, the commit it was taken from and its checksum, and that this admin's own decisions are document 12.
Before the copy each is read for a name, a number, an address or a password that should not be repeated here; the secret scan runs over them like over every file.

A check, `scripts/verify-code-references.mjs`, lists what the code names and fails when a decision number, a numbered document or a requirement code is in none of the three and not in this repository's own documents. What it cannot resolve is listed once, by hand, with the reason.
tests: The check passes on the repository as it is after the copy, and names every mention it had to leave unresolved.

The check's own test changes one thing at a time in a copy: a decision number that does not exist, a requirement code of an unknown family, a document removed. Each time the check must fail and name the file and the line.
lines.against: With `07-DECISIONS.md` taken out of a copy, the check fails and names D-58 with the first file that mentions it.
lines.back: Three documents and one script; putting the commit back removes them. No code changes.

rounds.name: The dashboard
rounds.why: P1. The first screen every person sees. In the order you set for the design work it comes before the areas (DL-008).

lines.found: The dashboard is one component with one view: figures for a period, six live queues, what needs attention, the pipeline, new leads, recent activity.
build: Each block becomes a widget under one contract: who may see it and with which module, its figure, its link, and its states: loading, empty, error, no access.

The missing widgets: the sales funnel with its conversion rate; overdue amounts by age and payables due; the health and milestones of projects. Every chart states its dates, its currency and its definition.
A widget whose module is switched off is absent, not empty.
tests: For every widget with a figure: its link opens a list of exactly that many rows. The records are made in the test, some of them at the edges of the period in Pakistan time.
Every widget in every state. A widget that fails shows its own error, and the rest of the dashboard is still drawn.
As each role: only the widgets that role may see. With a module off, its widget is not in the page.
The number of database queries the dashboard makes is written down as a limit.
browser: The crawl as four roles at both widths.
A journey step follows two figures to their lists and compares the numbers on the screen.
lines.against: With one widget's count changed to include one more state, the first test fails.
lines.back: Views and queries that only read. No record changes.

rounds.name: Without a mouse; help, pinned and recent screens
rounds.why: T-054 is P1, and the accessibility review of gate A waits for it. The new entries of the top bar get their keyboard tests from the first day.

lines.found: The search opens with Ctrl+K and answers to the arrow keys and Escape. The journeys press Ctrl+K once and Escape three times. No task is done by keyboard alone: the sidebar, the focus inside a dialog and the announcing of a refused field are untested.
build: A third journey, done by keyboard only: sign in; the sidebar, a group opened and a link followed; the search opened, a screen found, chosen, and Escape giving the focus back; a dialog and a drawer that keep the focus inside and return it; a lead and a quotation made; a refused field announced where it stands.
What the journey finds is corrected in the same round.
tests: The journey runs with the other two, in the sandbox and in CI.
A test reads every dialog for its name, and every field with an error for the link to its message.
lines.against: With the dialog no longer keeping the focus inside, the journey fails at that step.
lines.back: Tests, and small corrections to views.
lines.yours: After it, one person of your team does the same without a mouse, and with a screen reader if one is at hand. Gate A asks for that review.

lines.found: The top bar has the search, "Create new", the colour theme, the notifications and the account. It has no help entry, and no pinned or recent screens. A person's record has no place for such preferences yet.
build: A Help entry in the top bar: what this screen is for, the keyboard shortcuts, and the request number to give when asking for help.
A screen can be pinned from its heading; pinned screens stand at the head of the menu. The screens opened last are listed, for each person.
Both are kept with the person, in one small table added by a migration.
tests: Pinned and recent screens are remembered for each person and are still there after signing out and in.
Nobody is shown another person's; a screen the person may no longer open is not offered.
All of it by keyboard, in the journey of T-054.
browser: The crawl at both widths; the keyboard journey pins a screen and opens it from the menu.
lines.against: With the check of the person's rights taken out, "is not offered" fails.
lines.back: One migration that only adds; its way back removes the table.

rounds.name: Every shared part on one screen; a slow list and a lost connection
rounds.why: Both waited for the shared table (T-041), and both are P2. The first is a criterion of gate A ("shared component examples"). The second finishes the five states: the table can say "loading" since 20 November and no screen says it.

lines.found: No screen shows the shared parts side by side. The parts are 25 files in `platform/resources/views/components/admin` and the three parts of the table beside them; their rules are written there since 20 November (`README.md`). A new screen is a 69th destination: the registry of destinations, Feature status and the tests that count destinations change with it.
build: One screen under System, for owner and admin: every shared part in each of its states, drawn by the part itself with sample values, never by a copy of its markup. Buttons, badges, cards, fields with and without an error, the empty state, the dialog, the toast, the page links, and the table in its five states.
The destination is added to the registry with its permission, so that the menu, Feature status and the route agree.
tests: The screen opens for owner and admin and is refused to the other roles.
A test lists the files under `components/admin`: a part that is not drawn on the screen, and is not on a short written list of parts that cannot stand alone, fails it.
